subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

Losing my job turned out to be __an unexpected benefit__ because it pushed me to start my own business, which has been more successful than I ever imagined.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. "a blessing in disguise".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"a blessing in disguise"** means something that initially seems bad or unfavorable but turns out to have a positive outcome. (छुपा हुआ वरदान)

 
 
• **Example:** Losing his flight turned out to be a blessing in disguise as he avoided a major accident.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, losing the job, though initially perceived as bad, led to starting a successful business, which is a positive outcome. Therefore, "a blessing in disguise" is the most appropriate substitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: A golden opportunity** (सुनहरा अवसर): A chance to do something that is likely to be very successful or rewarding.

 
 
• **Example:** Winning the scholarship was a golden opportunity for her to study abroad.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: A diamond in the rough** (अनगढ़ हीरा): A person or thing with exceptional potential but needing refinement.
 
 
• **Example:** The young recruit is a diamond in the rough; he just needs proper training to shine.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: A mixed blessing** (मिश्रित वरदान): Something that has both good and bad aspects.
 
 
• **Example:** Having a big family is a mixed blessing; you get a lot of love but also a lot of responsibilities.
